sources.title: Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin: Brief History
sources.note: Official indexed history: Wisconsin and neighboring Michigan/Illinois, treaty land loss, Keshena government and 1973 restoration. Does not turn the asserted 10,000-year cultural history into an exact state founding.

sources.title: Milwaukee Public Museum: Menominee
sources.note: Direct original. Explicit Menominee/Menomini spelling equivalence, seasonal housing, French trade and nineteenth-century treaty narrative. Excludes inaccurate claim that only two tribes underwent federal termination and oversimplified universal end of sovereignty.

sources.title: Dartmouth College: Intensive ancestral Menominee farming at Sixty Islands (2025)
sources.note: Original university release, June 5, 2025, fully indexed; direct access 403. Reports McLeester et al., Science 388, pp. 1082 to 1085, DOI 10.1126/science.ads1643. Ridged fields, approximately 1000 to 1600, 2023 excavation and radiocarbon dating. Two passages combined under 200 words.

sources.title: College of Menominee Nation: The Menominee Clans Story
sources.note: Directly indexed college account of clan origins and responsibilities. Presented as the community’s explanation, not immutable duties of every individual.

sources.title: Milwaukee Public Museum: Wild Rice
sources.note: Direct original. Great Lakes practice explicitly includes Menominee and Ojibwe. Avoids treating the text’s single botanical species name as exhaustive or universalizing every practice.

sources.title: Menominee Indian Tribe: Termination and Restoration Timeline
sources.note: Direct original: 1954 law, 1961 implementation, Keshena hospital closure, 1964 petition, DRUMS, 1973 restoration. Excludes anachronistic 1931 IRA entry.

sources.title: Adrian Miller: Forest Management, the Menominee Tribe, Culture, and Traditional Knowledge (2023)
sources.note: Direct primary proceedings paper, printed pp. 5 to 6, from 2021 Northern Hardwood Conference. Author was Menominee Tribal Enterprises president. Uses management approach, not promotional superlatives or large aggregate timber claims.

sources.title: College of Menominee Nation: Sustainable Development Institute
sources.note: Original indexed account, institute established 1993 and work connecting governance, commerce, education and resource management.

sources.title: Christine Lemley and John Teller: Menominee Language Revitalization
sources.note: Direct primary chapter in Honoring Our Elders, printed pp. 161 to 182. Interviews 2004 to 2005 and program description in 2010. Writing witness printed p. 168, PDF index 7: Maec waewaenen / Thank you very much.

sources.title: University of Wisconsin Extension: Harvest of the Moon (2021 report)
sources.note: Indexed original report by Jennifer Gauthier, August 2021. May distribution of 25 sets, Daniel Grignon art, recipes and classroom materials. Future teacher plans are not described as completed outcomes.

sources.title: American Museum of Natural History: Kwakwa̱ka̱’wakw
sources.note: Direct original exhibition with community consulting curator Trevor Isaac. Multiple named nations; mask catalog 16/8942 and feast dish 16/8527 A,B. Avoids older usage that extends Kwakiutl indiscriminately to Haisla/Heiltsuk/Wuikinuxv.

sources.title: U’mista: Living Tradition, The Kwakwaka’wakw Potlatch
sources.note: Community cultural education resource, indexed original. Witnesses, gifts, wealth and coppers; contemporary household gifts distinguished from earlier examples.

sources.title: U’mista Cultural Centre: History of the Potlatch Collection
sources.note: Direct original. 1870s saltery, 1884 amendment, 1921 Dan Cranmer potlatch and 1922 prosecution, 1951 ban deletion and repatriation. The page’s 1952 Mungo Martin public potlatch date conflicts with 1953 museum report; that event date is not used here.

sources.title: U’mista Cultural Centre: T̕sit̕sikala̱m, April 2020
sources.note: Direct original newsletter entry published on website November 9, 2020. Sun mask long-term loan in July 2019, 1979/1980 cultural centre openings. Loan is not misrepresented as outright ownership transfer.

sources.title: Deur, Turner, Dick, Sewid-Smith and Recalma-Clutesi: Subsistence and Resistance (2013)
sources.note: BC Studies 179, pp. 13 to 37. Repository metadata direct; repository PDF cache miss. Full author-uploaded primary text read at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/308719395_Subsistence_and_Resistance_on_the_British_Columbia_Coast_Kingcome_Village%27s_Estuarine_Gardens_as_Contested_Space . Original publisher https://ojs.library.ubc.ca/index.php/bcstudies/article/view/184182/184173 . Two passages use figure caption, pp. 27 to 30 and 34, not unverified botanical processing details.

sources.title: British Columbia Provincial Museum: Annual Report 1953, The New Kwakiutl House
sources.note: Original museum annual report fully indexed under The New Kwakiutl House; direct PDF access failed. Contemporary witness to Mungo Martin’s family crest house, posts, hand-hewn framing and cedar boards; does not universalize every house size.

sources.title: U’mista Cultural Centre: Cheryl Wadhams
sources.note: Direct first-person artist statement. Exact attested modern sample dagans dlu t’sigwanu uses straight apostrophe in original: dagans dlu t'sigwanu / Socks & eggs. Family affiliations and 2016 language enrollment stated by artist.

sources.title: Fisheries and Oceans Canada: ’Namgis First Nation, Gwa’ni Hatchery
sources.note: Direct institutional account, modified November 5, 2015. Project began 1978; species-specific incubators, troughs and ponds. Avoids conflicting facility construction dates among sources.

sources.title: Burke Museum: In the Spirit of the Ancestors, Collage and Prints
sources.note: Archived institutional exhibition, original indexed. Charlie James and Ellen Neel’s 1927 watercolor crest series, and Doug Cranmer’s River Monster silkscreen 1992, catalog 1996-48/1. Does not apply other nations’ objects on page to Kwakwaka’wakw.

sources.title: Kwakiutl Band Council: Housing Department
sources.note: Official indexed description of renovation, repair, new construction and Fort Rupert emergency planning. Specific contemporary Kwakiutl community, not all Kwakwaka’wakw nations.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Recommend one narrative for explicitly documented alternate spellings of the same people; preserve imported phase dates.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: menomini 1530 to 1783, decoded bbox [-88.6671,44.8847,-83.7422,46.7493]; menominee 1492 to 1500, bbox [-91.7451,42.9239,-86.5935,46.0041]. Broad Great Lakes polygons extend beyond the core Menominee River/Wisconsin homeland; public caveat retained.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: Not a claim that every place in either outline was exclusive Menominee territory. Archaeological field evidence describes the specific ancestral Sixty Islands landscape, not all Great Lakes cultures.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: One broad cultural-linguistic record, explicitly multiple distinct nations rather than a centralized polity; no aliases added.
batchIdentityNotes.mapEvidence: Index 1492 to 1650. Decoded world1492 multipolygon bbox [-128.4403,49.5321,-124.2210,51.7745], northern Vancouver Island and nearby mainland coast.
batchIdentityNotes.limitations: Specific evidence attributed to G̱wawa̱’enux̱w, Kingcome, ’Namgis, Fort Rupert/Kwakiutl or named artists. Does not absorb neighboring Haisla, Heiltsuk, Wuikinuxv or other nations. Map dates retained only as coverage.
